title: Integral domain of short intermediate words
statement: Fix l, E, a scheme family, input locations and Operations [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. Let K be integral inputs satisfying Admissible with common intervals, and let B be a word of length at most two whose every system vertex satisfies Word.admissible. Then its actual integralValue is finite-Tor bounded constructible and derived complete [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], or is equal to the scalar tensor unit at its scheme. The conclusion is a property of one object and asserts no completion-map isomorphism.

proof.text: For a normalized admissible system M and an isomorphism A ≅ L(M), unrestricted normalized reconstruction makes L(M) complete and the actual counit R(L(M)) → M invertible. Transport completeness along the isomorphism, and use the intrinsic/legacy completeness equivalence. Reduction of the isomorphism followed by the counit identifies R(A) with M. Evaluating and using reductionEvaluation identifies each finite scalar reduction of A with the corresponding level of M. Isomorphism closure transports intrinsic constructibility. Homology isomorphisms transport the supplied common cohomological interval; composing each representative isomorphism in the definition of Tor amplitude transports the supplied common Tor interval. These give finiteTorConstructibleIntegral(A) directly.

proof.text: Induct on a word, retaining an isomorphism from its integral evaluation to the total limit of its system evaluation. For an input, completeness in Admissible makes the actual reconstruction unit invertible. For a scalar unit, the native ringed tensor comparison identifies the chosen monoidal unit with the rank-one constant completed coefficient object, which is complete. Reconstruction and the supplied unitReduction isomorphism give the required realization at that leaf. Completeness is transported along the explicit isomorphism of augmented Roos triangles.

proof.text: At a tensor vertex, apply the defining global quotient-tower tensor comparison, then total limit of system tensor applied to the two child reduction isomorphisms. Each child reduction isomorphism is reduction of its induction isomorphism followed by the effective counit. The pullback case is the same construction with one slot and the defining global pullback comparison. Proper image is total limit of system pushforward of reduction by definition, so functorial transport of the child reduction isomorphism suffices. Recursive admissibility supplies normalization at each child; no preservation assertion for unrelated systems is needed.

proof.text: For an open vertex, the first step applied to its child realization gives the finite-Tor integral domain. Open reconstruction effectivity makes both the actual reduction mate and the reconstruction unit at its open extension invertible. Compose that unit, total limit of the inverse mate, and total limit of open extension of the child reduction isomorphism. This gives the induction isomorphism for the open vertex, including identity and empty opens. Finally apply the first step to the root system and return the left disjunct of the assigned conclusion. The induction works for every finite word under the given recursive admissibility, so specializes to length at most two without changing the statement.

lean.statement:
theorem shortWordIntegralDomain
    {S : Type s} (W : S → Scheme.{u}) {I : Type i} (location : I → S)
    (o : Operations l E) {a : S} (B : Word W location a) (hLength : B.length ≤ 2)
    (K : ∀ k : I, DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E (W (location k))))
    (lo hi torLo torHi : ℤ)
    (hAdm : ∀ k : I, Admissible l E
      (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E (W (location k))) (K k) lo hi torLo torHi)
    (hIntermediate : Word.admissible l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi B) :
    finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E (W a) (B.integralValue l E W location o K) ∨
      B.integralValue l E W location o K =
        (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus l E (W a)).integralClosed.monoidal.tensorUnit
